signals.source_text: The Department of Aerospace Science and Technology - Politecnico di Milano will host Dr Joseph Pellettiere PhD PE for the seminar “Crashworthiness Testing at the Federal Aviation Administration”. 📅 13 October 2026 🕚 11:00–12:00 📍 Sala Consiglio DAER The #FAA has established a range of requirements to protect aircraft occupants in the event of an emergency landing, covering cabin interiors, seating systems and aircraft structural performance. During the seminar, Dr Pellettiere will present the FAA’s research into aircraft crashworthiness and the effects of different emergency landing conditions, reviewing a selection of impact tests conducted over the years through both in-house and sponsored research. Among the case studies presented will be the full-scale impact test of a Fokker 100 conducted at the NASA Langley Research Center pendulum facility. Dr Pellettiere supports the development and application of occupant injury criteria for aerospace systems and contributes to certification programmes involving aircraft structures, seats, cabin interiors and small unmanned aircraft systems. 🔗 More information: https://lnkd.in/e6DYnb4y #Polimi #DAER #AerospacePolimi

signals.source_text: Wow, September was an incredible month filled with new adventures. Hello October, I’m ready for you! I haven’t been posting quite as much lately because I’ve been laser-focused on my new role with Joby Aviation .✈️ Two months ago, I looked at my friends at a networking event and said, “The next time I stand here, I’ll be working for Joby Aviation.” That hadn’t happened yet. I call it prayer. Some call it manifesting. Call it what you want, but there is something powerful about believing in what’s possible before you can see how it will all come together. Sometimes we have to trust the process even when the process doesn’t make sense. Often what’s on the other side looks different, and better than we imagined. The last month has been full. In just four weeks, I dove headfirst into workforce development, began pilot school, attended multiple events, met with partners, and learned from strong leaders and colleagues. I’m grateful for where this season is taking me, professionally and personally, and excited to keep learning and building. Cheers to October and continuing to dream big. 💙 📸Carmel Beach, California

signals.source_text: Dear friends, I am excited to share that I have officially completed my Master’s degree in Global Studies at Bard College ! 🎓 The Bard MA Global Studies program has been a truly transformative experience, combining academic learning with practical internship opportunities. Although the program lasted only nine months, it was an incredibly enriching journey. I had the privilege of taking courses such as Diplomacy, National Security, and International Relations Theory, among many others, which deepened my understanding of global affairs and strengthened my passion for the field. I am deeply grateful to Bard College for this opportunity. I would especially like to thank Michelle K. Murray , Josie Snider , James Ketterer , Nassim AbiGhanem and rest of the faculty for their continuous guidance and support, as well as my fellow classmates for making this journey so memorable and rewarding. As I begin this next chapter, I am actively seeking job and internship opportunities in the New York City area, particularly in international relations, diplomacy, and related fields. I would greatly appreciate any leads, recommendations, or connections!
